rv.q: Zeldin, who directs, invites us to ponder the artificiality of theatre and the unreliability of memory.
Theatre Lyttelton’s stage currently conveys places and situations pivotal in the life experience of one particular Australian woman.
'The Confessions' is a thought-provoking new play which holds a mirror up to the face of life itself and to what it means to actually succeed in it.

cn.t: Critics praise this thought-provoking production for its exploration of memory's unreliability and life's deeper meanings, with Zeldin's direction inviting audiences to ponder theatre's artificiality and what it truly means to succeed.
